functions.get_item(sku: str) -> dict | None: returns {"sku": str, "name": str, "price": float (dollars, e.g. 12.5 = $12.50), "category": str}; None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id: str) -> dict |: returns {"id": str, "name": str, "discount": float (fraction, e.g. 0.10 = 10%), "region": str (state code, e.g. "TX")}; None if id unknown

why: Exposes item price (float dollars), customer discount (fraction) and region (state code) so invoice.py can pass region to tax.py. Unknown keys return None per team standard.

value: pricing.item_exists(sku) -> bool (True if sku is a known item). pricing.unit_price(sku) -> Decimal dollars, Decimal("0") if unknown. Called only when item_exists is True.
why: A price of 0 can be a real price, so existence needs its own boolean. Unknown sku detection must not rely on the 0 default.

value: pricing.customer_name(cid) -> str, "" if unknown (invoice then shows the id). pricing.discount_multiplier(cid) -> Decimal multiplier (10% off = Decimal("0.90")), Decimal("1") if unknown (0% off). Exception to the default-0 rule: a 0 multiplier would mean 100% off.
why: Follows team percent-as-multiplier standard. Default must be 1 (no discount), not 0 (everything free).

value: tax.compute_tax(customer_id, lines, subtotal, discount) -> (tax_amount, tax_multiplier). lines = list of (sku, Decimal line_amount) for known items only; subtotal and discount are Decimal dollars; discount is already rounded to cent. tax_amount is Decimal dollars rounded to cent. tax_multiplier is e.g. Decimal("1.0825") for 8.25%, Decimal("1") for 0%. Unknown customer returns (Decimal("0.00"), Decimal("1")). Tax module decides the taxable base.
why: invoice must not compute tax rules. Tax module owns base, rounding and rate. Invoice only formats percent from multiplier.

Conflicts with team standard: money must be integer cents (price should be int cents, e.g. 1250), and percentages must be percent numbers (discount should be 10 for 10%, not 0.10). Also 'None on unknown key' conflicts with our team rule that a lookup finding nothing raises KeyError. Please revise to: get_item -> {sku,name,price_cents:int,category}, raise KeyError if unknown; get_customer -> {id,name,discount_pct:float (10 = 10%),region:str|None} raise KeyError if unknown id. region None = no region on file.

functions.compute_tax_cents(lines: list[dict], reg: lines = [{"amount_cents": int, "category": str}, ...] (line totals before tax). Taxable amount = sum of amount_cents for lines whose category is NOT in exempt_categories.csv. base = taxable * (100 - discount_pct) / 100. tax = base * tax_pct / 100 rounded to nearest cent, half up (exact arithmetic, one rounding at the end). Returns int cents. region None (unknown customer / no region on file) -> tax 0. region not in rates.csv -> KeyError.
functions.tax_pct(region: str) -> float: percent number from rates.csv (8.25 = 8.25%). KeyError if region not listed.

why: Money in integer cents and percentages as percent numbers per team standard. Tax needs only region, line categories and discount_pct; it does not look up customers or items itself, so invoice.py passes those values in. RULES.md says unknown customer pays 0%; we map that to region=None -> 0 because tax cannot see customer records. Please object if you want another signal for unknown customer.

Also tax should not need item/customer lookups beyond what invoice passes in: proposed signature compute_tax_cents(lines: list[{amount_cents:int, category:str}], region: str|None, discount_pct: float) -> int. Invoice passes category from pricing.get_item and region/discount from pricing.get_customer. region None (unknown customer) -> 0. Unknown region -> KeyError. See message to team for the full version.
